blogs.title: Christmas Cookies- Bake the World a Better Place!
blogs.old_content:
The Christmas chocolate cookies are known to be brought by the Dutch in early 17th century. Christmas cookies are the most delicious during the holiday, the little chocolate chips acts as the beautiful shining stars on a night sky. The point is cookies are universally loved snacks that are just perfect for Christmas. Apart from Chocolate chip Cookies; butter cookies Pillsbury & Grinch cookies are also famous. In this blog we will comprehensively formulate the origin, tradition and process of making an appetizing plate of our favourite Christmas special Chocolate Chip Cookies.

Picture courtesy – Google

Most origins of American foods and dishes are unknown, but chocolate chip cookies are known to be invented by Ruth Wakefield, who ran the popular Toll House restaurant in Whitman, Massachusetts, with her husband, Kenneth, from 1930 to 1967, brought the Toll House Chocolate Crunch Cookie into being in the late nineteen-thirties. The chocolate bytes engulfed cookie by Ruth gave a sense of hope to the starved and poverty-fed crowd of Great Depression.

 

            Picture courtesy – Google

 

Here’s a quick recipe to make a plate of these chocolate fantasy delights-

Ingredients that you will need-

  • 1 cup butter(softened)
  • 1 cup white sugar
  • 2 eggs
  • 2 teaspoons of Vanilla Extracts
  • 1 cup brown sugar
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • 2 cups semi sweet chocolate chips
  • 1 cup chopped walnuts

The above mentioned ingredients should be arranged beforehand starting the process.

 

 

 

 

            Picture courtesy – Google

Directions

Instructions Checklist

  • STEP-1

Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

  • STEP-2

Cream together the butter, white sugar, and brown sugar until smooth. Beat in the eggs one at a time, and then stir in the vanilla. Dissolve baking soda in hot water. Add to batter along with salt. Stir in flour, chocolate chips, and nuts. Drop by large spoonfuls onto ungreased pans.

  • STEP-3

Bake for about 10 minutes in the preheated oven, or until edges are nicely browned

 

            Picture courtesy – Google

 

 

The Tradition attached to Christmas-

Ho ho ho!! The Santa’s catchphrase is synonymic with smell of freshly bakes Chocó-chip cookies as prominent as you can smell it. It seems like Cookies are an integral part of the family tradition on a Christmas Eve, but how it all started-Setting out milk and cookies for Santa is a tradition rooted in celebrations of Saint Nicholas, a third-century bishop who was also known for his kindness to children, so on the eve of Saint Nicholas Day (December 6th), children put out food for him—and what better fuel for a night's work than Christmas cookies and milk?

Christmas cookies, as we know them today, traces their roots to these Medieval European recipes. Dutch and German settlers introduced cookie cutters, decorative moulds, and festive holiday decorations to America. The act of leaving a treat out for Santa was born during the Great Depression as a lesson from parents to children on giving.

Butter cookies have more sugar and bake at a higher temperature than chocolate chip cookies. The amount of flour and sugar is increased, which means they will hold their shape better than Chocolate chip cookies .Butter cookies are great for rolling and cutting into shapes, offer a sturdier texture, and tend to ship well.

  • Grinch Cookies - Grinch Cookies are delicious cakey sugar cookies with a green hue and a candy sprinkle heart that are worth guzzling down a dozen, they are so tasty.

blogs.title: Is excessive entertainment harming the intellect of youth?
blogs.old_content:
This question has been hotly debated in the media, with some arguing that cinema is a great way to keep kids occupied while others argue that it has a negative effect on young adults. Cinema has been around for over 100 years and it's hard not to find yourself drawn in by its charm and appeal. It's hard to argue against the fact that it's an art form, but there are some harmful effects of cinema that need to be considered before deciding if it's a good idea for your child to watch or not.

The first thing to consider is whether or not you think the movies you watch are good for your child. If you think they aren't, then you should probably try another form of entertainment (i.e. reading books) until you've got a better grasp on what your child likes and dislikes about different forms of media (i.e. cartoons).

Another thing to consider is whether or not your child has watched/watched enough movies already this year so far; if they haven't then maybe it would be best if they didn't watch any more until next year, especially if they're still young and still growing up physically inside their bodies as well as mentally outside

 The rise of cinema has coincided with a decline in academic standards and a rise in mental illness among young adults. While there are many reasons for this trend, one of the most obvious is fan culture.

Fan culture is a term used to describe people who follow and participate in something for no other reason than to be part of it. Fan culture is often seen as positive, but it can also be toxic if not moderated properly. In fact, studies have shown that fan culture can lead to mental health issues like anxiety or depression.

Why cult fan bases are toxic

Cult fan bases are especially harmful because they encourage followers to engage with content on social media platforms such as Instagram and Twitter where they see less moderation than they would in real life. This means that these fans are more likely than non-fans to see things that might negatively affect their mental health: violent images, sexualized content (especially when it comes from celebrities), hate speech or other negative content being shared without context or explanation. When this happens regularly over time it can lead to feelings of alienation or isolation which can cause permanent damage to your mental health."

 

What is the purpose of entertainment?

The answer to this question is simple. Entertainment is an important part of human life, and it has many uses. For one thing, entertainment helps us to relieve stress and anxiety. It also keeps us from getting bored and gives us something to do when we get bored. For example, if you are in a boring situation or if you just need something to do when you are waiting for something else to happen, then watching TV or playing video games can be entertaining.

Another reason why humans need entertainment is because it keeps them from doing bad things. If there is no entertainment available then people will usually start doing bad things such as stealing money from others or committing crimes against other people who are not involved with their actions whatsoever. In this way, entertainment helps society stay safe by providing them with outlets where they can release their pent-up energy without being hurtful towards others in any way shape or form whatsoever!
